results.question: When do I send my first unemployment status report to Kela?
results.answer: In your first application, you report your unemployment dates starting from your first day of unemployment [S1]. To get your first benefit payment, you must submit an unemployment status report covering a period of 2 weeks after you have submitted your first application [S1][S6]. You can only report days that have already passed [S1][S3].

results.question: I'm 22 and have no vocational qualification. Do I have to apply for studies to get the benefit?
results.answer: Yes, if you are under 25 and do not have a vocational qualification or higher education degree, you must apply for admission to at least two education programmes that begin in the autumn term [S2][S5][S8]. You must also participate in any entrance exam you are invited to [S2][S8]. If you do not apply for admission to education, turn down a place of study, or stop your studies, an obligation to work will be imposed on you [S6][S7][S8].

results.question: How much pay subsidy can an employer get for hiring me if I have reduced work ability?

results.question: Can I get my travel costs paid when I go to an aptitude test for labour market training?
results.answer: Yes, if you are an unemployed jobseeker, you can apply for reimbursement of travel and accommodation expenses from the employment authority when travelling for an aptitude test or admission event for labour market training [S1][S4]. Travel and accommodation expenses for participating in a service can be reimbursed only if you are unemployed and registered as a jobseeker with the employment services in your area [S8]. Additionally, the employment authority must consider the reimbursement appropriate for the availability of labour and your employment [S8].

results.question: Kela paid me labour market subsidy before May 2026. Will they check my income now?
results.answer:
If Kela paid you labour market subsidy without a means test before you transferred to the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026, Kela will check your income by 30 September 2026 [S2]. 
This income check determines how much of your income affects the means test [S2]. 
Kela will contact you if necessary before applying the means test, and you will receive a separate decision notice if your benefit must be reduced [S2]. 
The means test only applies to future payments and will not reduce your general social security benefit retroactively [S2].

Note: The labour market subsidy was abolished when Kela began paying the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026. [S9]

results.question: what is yleistuki
results.answer: Yleistuki (the general social security benefit) is an unemployment benefit paid by Kela [S2][S5]. It is intended for unemployed jobseekers aged 18–64 who live permanently in Finland and who cannot get or have used up their earnings-related unemployment allowance [S5]. To get it, you must be registered as an unemployed jobseeker with employment services and be available for work on the labour market [S5][S6].
